content.thinking:
I'm working on the postmortem now, starting from the key facts: the HighErrorRate alert fired at 12:24, the errors began around 12:17, and things returned to normal by 12:25. I'm also noting the two deploys, the P2 at 12:17:36 and the earlier P1 at 08:17:36, along with the replica split at T10 where the rollout stalled halfway.

I'm tying the log errors to the cache format: the ValueError on '2400/8' comes from the old reader, which expects a bare cents figure, while the new revision writes that amount/items shape. Background ClientDisconnected noise predates the onset, and the account page error rate climbed from 0.5% to 24.5%, peaking at 12:18, before the rollback was confirmed.

I'm checking whether the new revision's entry format explains the '2400/8' value, since the generator fixture hands back the new-shaped entry. Next I'm looking at why the old replicas were still reading the cache: the P2 rollout stalled with three replicas on each revision, so both served against the same cache. I still need to rule out the earlier P1 deploy.

I'm checking the remaining rule-outs for the earlier P1 deploy: metrics from the 361 minutes before the alert show errors at the 1.0% baseline, the rollback to 5470c1a was confirmed with the service back to normal, and account pages rendered fine from 11:49 to 12:14. I'm also noting that the only flag changes in the hour before came from Argus, which leaves the P2 rollout as the root cause candidate.

I'm now checking whether the old replicas are the ones raising that error, since the new revision's reader returns None rather than raising, and whether the cache key stays the same across both revisions.

I'm settling the root cause now: the new revision changed what the summary cache holds, from a bare cents figure to an "amount/items" text shape, and the old reader raises a ValueError on that shape instead of falling back. That old-reader behavior is inferred from the diff and the log message, which is reasonably solid. I'm keeping the claim to what the diff and logs actually show.

I'm checking whether the writer of those entries is part of this repo, and whether the generator fixture shows the new shape being handed back for every lookup. I'll treat the new-format entries as something both revisions read from the shared cache, and cite the fixture as the source for that.

I'm working out the five-whys chain now: the old revision's reader hit entries in the new shape, because the new deploy changed what the summary cache holds while old replicas were still serving alongside it during the paused rollout.

Next I'm listing the contributing factors: the old reader raising instead of treating an unreadable entry as a miss, and the missing compatibility check that would have caught a cache shape change still readable by the revision serving alongside it. I'm drafting a CI item that runs the previous revision's reader against entries the new revision writes.

I'm weighing whether to list the rollout pause as a contributing factor, since the mixed-version window only existed while it was held, but I can't yet tell if it was already paused before onset, so I'm leaning toward leaving it out.

I'm listing the contributing factors now, starting with whether the rollout had any automated analysis that would have halted or reverted it once the error rate rose, which I haven't confirmed. If it didn't, progressive-delivery analysis that rolls back on an error-rate rise would be the fix. I'm also noting that nobody was paged, since the alert wasn't linked to an on-call incident, so routing HighErrorRate on io-shop to on-call paging would address that.

I'm settling on the action items now, weighing whether the pre-deploy compatibility check and the automatic halt on error-rate rises each answer a contributing factor, and whether the third item is still in progress.

I'm checking the remaining items: one for the on-call page on HighErrorRate, and the risk that rolling out revision 696c33a again, or writing entries in its shape where the old reader still runs, would reproduce the failure. I'm also weighing whether new-format entries left under bare shopper ids need deleting, which the notes flag.

I'm drafting the timeline section now, covering the symptom, the mixed-version rollout, the rollback, and the confirmation. I'm also noting which parts went well: the investigator tied onset to the P2 deploy, the mitigation rolled back, Argus ruled out flag changes, and Code-Fix flagged the outside-repo change its fix depends on.

I'm weighing which parts of the postmortem still need filling in: nothing obvious went wrong in the response, and the paused rollout is already covered as a contributing factor. I'm also checking whether the "is not a figure in cents" errors really came from the replicas on 5470c1a, which is still an inference I haven't confirmed.

I'm checking the P1 rule-out next: the service was healthy with 5470c1a in place, so the earlier deploy doesn't account for the onset. I'm also keeping the notes straight on what is inferred, like which replicas raised the "is not a figure in cents" errors and where the new-format entries came from, since the logs aren't split by revision.

I'm settling the root cause wording now: revision 696c33a changes what a summary cache entry holds, from a bare cents figure to amount/items text, and the older reader can't parse that new shape.

Now I'm checking the replicas still on 5470c1a: they read the same entries and raised ValueError on that text instead of treating it as a miss, which is what fails the account page. That settles the root cause, and it's grounded in the record, so I'm not treating it as an unrun reading.

action_items.item: Add a pre-deploy check, for every change to the format of a cached or stored entry, that runs the serving revision's reader against entries written in the candidate revision's format.
Add automated rollout analysis to io-shop's rolling updates that halts and reverts the rollout when the error rate rises while revisions are mixed.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's share of failed requests rose well above its usual level.
The failing account page requests raised ValueError when they read a summary cache entry, '{G3714.1}', that was not a figure in cents, in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py.

The cache held entries in the new 'amount/items' text format that revision 696c33a introduced, and the replicas reading them expected a bare cents figure. The new revision's own reader returns no error on text it cannot read, so the error comes from the reader in the earlier revision.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 of revision 5470c1a: the service was measured healthy with it in place. The metrics read before the onset showed the usual error rate, account pages rendered normally before the onset, and the service returned to normal after the confirmed rollback left 5470c1a running.
A feature flag change: the flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the window read.

causal_chain.step: Deploy P2 at {P2.1} rolled out revision 696c33a, which brought in the new entry format. As of {T10.1}, its rolling update was paused partway, with replicas on 696c33a and on 5470c1a both serving against the same cache.

Revision 696c33a changed the format of cache entries that the still-serving 5470c1a replicas also read, and the earlier revision's reader raised an error on the new format instead of treating it as a miss.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update changed the format of a saved summary of each shopper's spending, and the older version, still running beside the new one because the update stopped partway, could not read the new format and failed the account page.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen, before the change went out, that the revision already serving could read cache entries in the new revision's format.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The format mismatch would have been caught before deploy P2, and the account pages would not have failed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No automatic rollout analysis was seen that halted or reverted io-shop's rolling update when its error rate rose. The rollout stayed partway, with both revisions serving.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The mixed-revision state would have been reverted soon after the error rate rose, which would have shortened the failure.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been brought in as soon as the alert fired, instead of the response depending on automation alone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent found that the rollout of 696c33a was paused partway with both revisions serving, which tied the onset to deploy P2.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone but Argus, ruling flags out.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back io-shop's deployment off revision 696c33a.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed the rollback had brought the service back from the incident's level.
Code-Fix wrote a fix and said plainly that it helps only together with a change outside the repository, so no partial fix was kept.

input.root_cause: Revision 696c33a changed what a summary cache entry holds. It used to be a bare cents figure and is now 'amount/items' text (`_ENTRY_FORMAT`). The replicas still running 5470c1a read those same entries and raised ValueError on the new text in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py instead of treating it as a miss, so the account page request failed.
input.still_at_risk: Account pages could fail again if revision 696c33a goes out again while the earlier revision is still serving, or if cache entries in its new format are left where the earlier revision reads.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
